description: A team looking to do something innovative.
summary:
Orbitech Health Monitor is a web application for astronauts to monitor important health parameters during space missions. Crew members can set up a profile or log in, add readings for blood oxygen, temperature, blood glucose, total protein, cholesterol, haemoglobin and calcium, and have a history of measurements. The Monitor page displays current readings and identifies values that fall outside of the normal range for adults, and the Trends page displays changes over time. Each indicator is accompanied by a Risks & Warnings page that includes explanations of its importance, signs to look for, and when to get medical advice on board, and links to NASA and Canadian Space Agency research.

This project tackles the problem of going to space and monitoring their own health in the event and it simplifies the review of health information and promotes regular checks. This is because spaceflight hazards can have an impact on physical health and early detection can help crew members take the necessary steps to mitigate the risk.
details:
Orbitech Health Monitor is a health tracking application for use in a web browser that has been designed for astronauts during long duration spaceflight. Crew members can log in or create a profile and the health readings will be created and stored in the browser separately for each profile. The Monitor page shows the seven indicators - SpO₂, body temperature, blood glucose, total protein, total cholesterol, haemoglobin and calcium - and alerts to results above and below the normal range for adults. A Trends page plots saved readings versus time, and a Risks & Warnings page discusses the importance of each measure, symptoms to look for, and suggested next steps, including links to NASA and Canadian Space Agency research.

The project will help ease the burden on regular self-checks and make it more likely that crew members will notice changes early, particularly in the event of a lack of communication with Earth or access to medical support. Its visual dashboard combines measurements, trends and guidance in one place, and provides a clear, easy-to-use interface on all screens. It is implemented completely in HTML, CSS and JavaScript with the use of browser local storage to store profiles and readings, so it does not need any extra hardware. We took into account the hazards of spaceflight, units of measurement, context, readability, privacy of locally stored data and limits of research.
